chunks: "Hope and fear do not come together in a heart except that Jannah becomes obligatory for it. So when you perform salat, turn your heart toward Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for there is no believing servant who turns his heart toward Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in his salat and his du'a, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, turns toward him the hearts of the believers, and supports him—along with their love for him—with Jannah."

key_terms.الرَّغْبَةُ: hopeful desire for Allah’s mercy and reward
key_terms.الرَّهْبَةُ: fear of Allah’s displeasure and punishment
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the believers whose hearts Allah turns toward His servant
key_terms.دُعَائِهِ: his du'a, meaning his supplication to Allah
key_terms.قَلْبٍ: the inner heart as the locus of sincerity and devotion

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about hope, fear, and presence of heart in salat?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that a heart combining hope in Allah and fear of Him is a heart destined for Jannah. It also instructs the believer to be fully present in salat and du'a, promising that sincere turning toward Allah brings divine favor, the love of the believers, and Jannah.
